loops.description: Single-pass refinement loop: pick one issue, write one grounded user story, mark done

tasks.name: Select and reserve the oldest refine:pick issue
commandArgs: number=$(gh issue list --label "refine:pick" --state open --limit 1000 --json number --jq 'sort_by(.number) | .[0].number'); test -n "$number" || exit 75; body=$(gh issue view "$number" --json number,title,body --jq '{number,title,body}'); gh issue edit "$number" --add-label refine:doing --remove-label refine:pick >/dev/null; printf "%s\n" "$body"

tasks.name: AI: write one grounded user story without clarification questions
commandArgs: First, load all skills available for your current agent. Then rewrite GitHub issue {{number}} as a single autonomous refinement pass. Load and follow the @user-story skill to structure the issue as a development-ready user story, then apply @humanizer to the final prose. The feature to capture is: {{title}}. Context from the issue body: {{body}}. Ground the story in the actual codebase by reading relevant files. Never explore or read files outside the current repository root. Update the GitHub issue body yourself with the final user story in Mike Cohn As a/I want to/so that format, Gherkin Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, edge cases, and a Mermaid diagram if appropriate. Make reasonable assumptions from the issue and codebase; do not ask clarification questions, append questions, or create a question branch. Always apply the 'refine:done' label, remove 'refine:doing', and keep the final body as valid Markdown. Do not ask me anything during the session.

tasks.name: Verify: the single refinement is marked refine:done
commandArgs: labels=$(gh issue view {{number}} --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'); echo "$labels" | grep -qE '^refine:done$' && git checkout -- . && git clean -fd && exit 0 || exit 1

tasks.name: Recovery: return an incomplete refinement to refine:pick
Idle: no refine:pick issues are available
commandArgs: Nothing to refine, no issues with refine:pick label
